standard_prerequisites.name: Bielliptic quotient construction and real semi-algebraic connected components
standard_prerequisites.statement: The author uses the elliptic curve y^2=x(x+1)(x-t), its square and the specified fixed-point-free involution. Real connected components are semi-algebraic over the real Puiseux field; they are not Euclidean connected components over an arbitrary field.

core_obligations: Keep the exact real Puiseux field, quotient action and signs-property definition
Retain the entire specialization/sign-parity proof and attribution, not merely a statement that some nonarchimedean surface exists
Do not conflate signs-property failure on a bielliptic surface with EPT failure on the old K3 surface1926
proof_roadmap: Form the bielliptic quotient of the square of an explicit elliptic curve.
Assume a rational function separates the chosen real component from the others and pull it back to the product.
Use the four sign conjugates to obtain a polynomial with the prescribed quadrant signs.
Specialize to t=0 and use the conflicting parity of the x1 factor to contradict the sign pattern.
difficulty_reason: H2: the short proof requires a nonroutine explicit free-involution quotient of an elliptic product and a carefully chosen real component, followed by a rational-function sign-symmetrization and degeneration whose quadrant pattern forces contradictory factor parity. This is a concrete geometric counterexample with its complete author argument, not a routine restatement of the signs definition. It is different from the K3/EPT construction.
